prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: finished illustrated world travel map for the Toli.me personal website, landscape 3:2, high-resolution raster.
Primary request: Repaint the actual world map in reference image 1 as a beautiful, clean hand-painted travel atlas in the warm cream and dark forest-green storybook style of reference image 2. This is the travel map itself, not a screenshot of a website and not a UI mockup.

Input images: Image 1 is the GEOGRAPHY AND VISITED-COUNTRY SOURCE. Preserve its real continental/country geometry and exact set of fourteen blue-highlighted countries, but replace its dark background and blue-gray palette. Remove all source UI controls. Image 2 is a STYLE REFERENCE only: warm ivory paper, expressive dark forest ink, restrained watercolor, elegant serif title, a little handmade warmth, generous open space. Do not copy its page, people, book, envelope, menu, or comic.

Composition: One large, geographically recognizable world map centered on an ivory paper canvas (#fcfaf1), with Americas left, Europe/Africa center, Asia/Australia right. No frame. Airy and uncluttered; no tiny city scenes. Continents are pale taupe with very fine soft pencil country boundaries. The fourteen visited countries alone are softly watercolor-painted sage/forest green; all other countries remain pale ivory/taupe. Flat editorial atlas, no perspective, no floating fantasy islands. Geographic proportions and coastlines should follow source image 1 closely.
Top-left generous title area, elegant dark green serif text exactly: "Places I’ve been". Small subtitle beneath exactly: "A little of the world I’ve explored."
All fourteen visited countries must have exactly one clear, readable name label on the map, with delicate leader lines when needed to avoid overlap, no numbered keys:
"Canada", "United States", "Nicaragua", "Costa Rica", "Finland", "France", "Italy", "Russia", "Israel", "Tanzania", "Thailand", "Vietnam", "Malaysia", "Australia".
Place labels in geographically sensible positions, with countries in crowded Europe and Southeast Asia labeled just offshore through short, clean leader lines. Use forest-green lettering. Avoid multiple overlapping label lines.

Geography constraints: Only these exact fourteen countries are highlighted. Greenland remains unhighlighted, separate from Canada. Alaska is part of the United States. Do not add a Hawaii pin. Nicaragua is north of Costa Rica, not Panama. Finland is east of Sweden; do not shade Sweden or Norway. France and Italy remain distinct. Israel is a small precise country callout on the eastern Mediterranean, never a large region. Malaysia includes the peninsula and northern Borneo portions, not Indonesia. Thailand and Vietnam are distinct, with Laos and Cambodia unhighlighted. Tanzania lies in East Africa south of Kenya, not Madagascar. Russia spans northern Europe and Asia. No South American country is highlighted. China, India, Japan, Mexico and New Zealand stay unhighlighted.
Footer-left understated small green paint-swatch legend with exact words "Visited"; beside it small readable caption exactly "14 countries from my travel archive". No other statistics.
Style: Fine organic ink coastlines, subtle watercolor grain and warm paper texture, pale sage wash in visited countries, highly legible labels. A tiny unobtrusive hand-drawn compass rose in empty lower-left ocean is acceptable. Plenty of empty ocean, no busy roads or scenery.
Avoid: route lines, flight paths, dates, city pins, city-specific monuments, implied trip chronology, unverified destinations, photographs, cartoon people, crowded decorative objects, vintage distressed stains, UI controls, web navigation, gradients, 3D, drop shadows, watermark. This is a stylish personal travel archive illustration, not a navigation chart.
